renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: dtu_volcano
  title: Transcript usage volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a transcript in one contrast: the log2 fold change of its usage within its gene on the horizontal axis and its adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers which isoforms gain or lose share of their gene's expression between conditions, and how confidently.
    How to read: points in the upper right gain usage in the treatment and points in the upper left lose it. Usage is relative to the other isoforms of the gene, so an isoform can change without any change in the gene's total expression. Open the table tile to see the gene behind a labelled transcript.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, the cut-off the catalog recipe uses for the significant, up and down calls (its fdr parameter). The DEXSeq vignette illustrates a 10% false discovery rate instead, so 0.05 is the stricter choice. No fold-change line is drawn because the calls use none.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DEXSeq/inst/doc/DEXSeq.html
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 0.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Usage log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: transcript_id
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: padj
    label: gene_id
    category: direction

- component: card
  title: Transcripts by usage call
  description: |-
    Each unit is one transcript tested in one contrast, and the ring splits them into gain, loss and not significant. The second figure counts the distinct transcripts. It answers how many isoforms change usage overall.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly not significant means few isoform switches, or too little replication to detect them. Open the volcano to see the borderline transcripts.
    Lines and annotations: a transcript is called when its adjusted p-value is below 0.05, the catalog recipe default, and the direction is the sign of its usage log2 fold change.
  column: transcript_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: transcripts, by usage call

- component: card
  title: Usage change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of usage log2 fold changes over all transcripts and contrasts in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the usage shifts are.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means most isoforms keep their share and a few switch strongly. A median is not shown as a hero because gains and losses cancel to about zero. Filter to one contrast to compare them.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: usage log2 fold change, with its spread

- component: interactive
  title: Usage call
  description: |-
    Pick one or more usage calls (up, down, not significant) to restrict every tile of the tab to those transcripts. It answers which isoforms gain or lose usage when you only want one side.
    How to read: select up and down together to hide the unchanged transcripts, then read the volcano and the table on the significant ones only.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: direction

- component: table
  title: Transcript usage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a transcript in one contrast with its mean expression, usage log2 fold change, p-value, adjusted p-value, the gene-level q-value and the call. It answers which transcripts and genes to follow up, and a row selection filters the rest of the dashboard to that gene.
    How to read: sort by adjusted p-value, then check the gene-level q-value, which controls the false discovery rate per gene rather than per transcript. A gene with several significant isoforms is a stronger candidate than a single one.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DEXSeq/inst/doc/DEXSeq.html
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: exon_volcano
  title: Exon usage volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene in one contrast: the usage log2 fold change of its most significant exonic bin on the horizontal axis and the gene-level q-value on the vertical axis. It answers which genes use their exons differently between conditions.
    How to read: genes high on the plot have at least one exon used differently, and the horizontal position says in which direction the strongest bin moves. A gene can be significant with a small fold change when many bins shift a little. Open the table tile to see how many bins were tested and called.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a gene-level q-value of 0.05, the cut-off the catalog recipe uses for its calls (its fdr parameter). The DEXSeq vignette illustrates a 10% false discovery rate and describes the gene-level q-value as controlling the FDR per gene. No fold-change line is drawn because the calls use none.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DEXSeq/inst/doc/DEXSeq.html
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 0.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Top exon usage log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 gene-level q-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene_id
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: padj
    category: direction
    label: gene_id

- component: card
  title: Genes by exon usage call
  description: |-
    Each unit is one gene in one contrast, and the ring splits them by the direction of their strongest exon shift, or not significant. The second figure counts the distinct genes. It answers how many genes change exon usage.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly not significant means little differential exon usage. A strong imbalance between up and down usually reflects which bin is the most significant, not a gene-wide trend.
    Lines and annotations: a gene is called when its gene-level q-value is below 0.05, the catalog recipe default.
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: genes, by exon usage call

- component: card
  title: Significant exonic bins
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of exonic bins called significant across genes and contrasts, and the bars split it by the direction of each gene's strongest bin. The strip gives the largest and the median count per gene. It answers how widespread the exon changes are within genes.
    How to read: a high maximum points to a gene with many shifted bins, often a real isoform switch. A median near zero is normal, since most genes change at no bin.
    Lines and annotations: a bin is called with the adjusted p-value cut-off of 0.05 used by the catalog recipe.
  column: bins_significant
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - max
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: direction
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: significant bins, by call

- component: card
  title: Size of the strongest exon shift
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median absolute usage log2 fold change of each gene's most significant bin, and the box shows its quartiles. It answers how large the exon shifts are, whatever their direction.
    How to read: a high median means the strongest bins move a lot. The absolute value is used so that gains and losses do not cancel out.
  column: abs_log2fc
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: absolute log2 fold change, with its spread

- component: interactive
  title: Exon usage call
  description: |-
    Pick one or more calls (up, down, not significant) to restrict every tile of the tab to those genes. It answers which genes remain when you only want one side.
    How to read: select up and down together to hide the unchanged genes before reading the volcano and the table.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: direction

- component: table
  title: Exon usage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene in one contrast: how many exonic bins were tested and called, the most significant bin with its usage log2 fold change, and the gene-level q-value. It answers which genes to follow up, and a row selection filters the rest of the dashboard to that gene.
    How to read: sort by q-value and read the bin counts beside it. A gene with several significant bins is a stronger candidate than one with a single bin.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DEXSeq/inst/doc/DEXSeq.html
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: volcano
  title: Transcript usage volcano
  description: |-
    Each point is a transcript: its usage log2 fold change between the two conditions on the horizontal axis and the gene-level adjusted q-value of its gene on the vertical axis. It answers which isoforms change share within their gene, and how confidently.
    How to read: points in the upper right gain usage and points in the upper left lose it. Every transcript of a gene shares one q-value, so the points of one gene line up horizontally. Open the table tile to see the gene behind a labelled transcript.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is a gene-level q-value of 0.05, the cut-off the catalog recipe uses for the significant, up and down calls. The DEXSeq vignette illustrates a 10% false discovery rate and describes the gene-level q-value as controlling the FDR per gene. No fold-change line is drawn because the calls use none.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DEXSeq/inst/doc/DEXSeq.html
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 0.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Usage log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 gene-level adjusted q-value
  roles:
    feature_id: feature_id
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: padj
    category: direction
    label: gene_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: qq
  title: P-value QQ plot
  description: |-
    Each point is a transcript: its observed raw p-value, as minus log10, against the value expected if no isoform changed usage. It answers whether the test statistics are well calibrated.
    How to read: points hugging the diagonal for most of the range and lifting off at the far end mean a few real signals over a calibrated null. A curve that leaves the diagonal early, or sits below it, points to inflation or deflation from a wrong design, batch effects or low counts.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, the expectation when p-values are uniformly distributed under no effect. The shaded band is the 95% confidence interval of that null, so points inside it are consistent with chance.
  kind: qq
  config:
    show_ci: true
    show_identity: true
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    p_value: pvalue
    feature_id: feature_id

- component: card
  title: Transcripts tested
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct transcripts tested, and the bars rank the usage calls (up, down, not significant) by how many transcripts each holds. It answers how large the tested set is and how it splits.
    How to read: a leading not significant bar is the usual case. A strong imbalance between up and down is worth checking against the sample design.
    Lines and annotations: the call uses a gene-level adjusted q-value below 0.05, the catalog recipe default.
  column: feature_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: direction
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: transcripts, by usage call

- component: card
  title: Calls by direction
  description: |-
    Each unit is one transcript, and the ring splits them into gain, loss and not significant. The second figure is the most common call. It answers how many isoforms change usage overall.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly not significant means few isoform switches, or too little replication to detect them. Open the volcano to see the borderline transcripts.
    Lines and annotations: the call uses a gene-level adjusted q-value below 0.05, the catalog recipe default.
  column: direction
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: direction
  caption: calls, by direction

- component: card
  title: Usage change spread
  description: |-
    The hero number is the range of usage log2 fold changes over all transcripts, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how large the usage shifts are.
    How to read: a box tight around zero with a long range means most isoforms keep their share and a few switch strongly. The range is shown instead of a median because gains and losses cancel to about zero.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: range
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: usage log2 fold change, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Transcript usage table
  description: |-
    Each row is a transcript with its gene, usage log2 fold change, p-value, gene-level adjusted q-value and call. It answers which transcripts and genes to follow up, and a row selection filters the rest of the dashboard to that transcript.
    How to read: sort by q-value, then look at the fold change to see which isoform gains share. A gene with several significant isoforms is a stronger candidate than a single one.
    Source: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/DEXSeq/inst/doc/DEXSeq.html
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: feature_id
